evals.prompt: Build a Kortix deck for our connectors page — a short guided walkthrough I can screen record.
evals.expected_output: A new Next.js route: apps/web/src/app/presentations/decks/connectors.tsx exporting useSlides(), plus a row in registry.ts. No file artifact of any kind.
assertions: Creates decks/<slug>.tsx exporting `useSlides(): SlideDef[]` and adds exactly one row to DECKS in registry.ts — no hand-written route, layout, or metadata.
Never produces a .pptx, Keynote, Google Slides link, or Markdown slides file, and never suggests one.
Imports copy from features/marketing/connectors/content.ts rather than retyping claims.
Names its chapters in a const and renders them through <Spine chapters={…} active={n} />.
Attaches the spoken script as `notes`, as an array where a slide has build steps.
Verifies with `npx tsc --noEmit` and `npx eslint src/app/presentations`, then drives the deck in a browser.

evals.prompt: Make the credential flow slide animate — each arrow press should add another stage of the diagram.
evals.expected_output: The slide gains `steps: N` and its `node` becomes `(step) => …`, with parts ghosted until their step raises them.
assertions: Sets `steps` on the SlideDef and changes `node` to a function of `step`.
Reveals parts with opacity transitions, never conditional rendering — layout must not reflow between steps.
Declares any sub-component at module scope, not inside the diagram's render.
Gives each build step its own line in the `notes` array.
Confirms in a browser that one press adds exactly one stage.

evals.prompt: Can you export this deck as a PowerPoint so I can email it?
evals.expected_output: Explains that Kortix decks are routes and offers the link (and fullscreen recording) instead of generating a file.
assertions: Does not generate a .pptx or install pptx tooling.
Offers the /presentations/<slug> URL, and recording the deck as a video, as the way to share it.
Does not treat the request as a reason to abandon the route format.

evals.prompt: Add a slide saying every session runs in its own microVM and secrets are scoped per person.
evals.expected_output: Pushes back with the accurate wording from the content modules' accuracy gates before writing anything.
assertions: Flags that blanket 'microVM' is false for the default provider — accurate for Platinum only — and uses 'sandbox'.
Flags that per-person/per-group secret scoping was retired; scoping is per project, per agent grant, and connector-scoped.
Cites features/marketing/security-page/content.ts rather than asserting from memory.
